# contentful Provider

Manages Contentful configuration and content within existing spaces with Terraform. The provider does not create or delete spaces.

## Authentication

Set `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_ACCESS_TOKEN` in the environment before running Terraform to avoid placing a Contentful Management API token directly in configuration. You can instead set the `access_token` provider attribute; a configured non-null value takes precedence over the environment variable. The provider reports an error if the resolved token is empty.

Most configurations should leave `url` unset and use the public Contentful Management API. Use `CONTENTFUL_URL` or the `url` provider attribute only when a different API base URL is required; a configured non-null `url` takes precedence over the environment variable.

Resources operate on existing Contentful spaces. Supply the required space IDs to individual resources; this provider does not create or delete spaces.

For a complete first configuration and plan, see [Getting started](guides/getting-started). For timeout defaults and environment-readiness behavior, see [Operation timeouts](guides/operation-timeouts).

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    contentful = {
      source = "cysp/contentful"
    }
  }
}

provider "contentful" {}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `access_token` (String, Sensitive) Contentful Management API access token. Set this attribute or the CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_ACCESS_TOKEN environment variable; a configured non-null value takes precedence. The provider requires a non-empty token when configured.
- `url` (String) Contentful Management API base URL. Defaults to the public Contentful Management API. Can also be set with the CONTENTFUL_URL environment variable; a configured non-null value takes precedence.
